question_content: pA manufacturing company has many IoT devices in facilities around the world. The company uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to collect data from the devices. The data includes device ID, capture date, measurement type, measurement value, and facility ID. The company uses facility ID as the partition key.pThe company's operations team recently observed many WriteThroughputExceeded exceptions. The operations team found that some shards were heavily used but other shards were generally idle.pHow should the company resolve the issues that the operations team observed?

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange the partition key from facility ID to a randomly generated key.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. If you use a universally unique identifier (UUID) as a partition key, it distributes incoming data records evenly across all shards in a stream. This solution reduces the likelihood of hot shards and increases overall throughput. The current facility ID partition key causes an uneven distribution of records.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/key-concepts.html#partition-key"partition keys/a. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/troubleshooting-producers.html"how to troubleshoot Kinesis Data Streams producers/a. pLearn more about href="https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/kinesis-data-stream-throttling"Kinesis Data Streams throttling/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIncrease the number of shards.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If you increase the number of shards, it does not resolve the underlying issue of uneven data distribution that is caused by selecting an incorrect partition key, such as facility ID. A disproportionate amount of records would be grouped and sent to the same shard that is based on the same facility ID. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-using-sdk-java-resharding.html"how to reshard a stream in Kinesis Data Streams/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pArchive the data on the producer's side.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If you archive data on the producer side, it might help throughput issues temporarily. However, this method does not address the root cause. The uneven distribution of records to shards would persist because you selected an incorrect partition key, such as facility ID.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-extended-retention.html"how to change the data retention period/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pChange the partition key from facility ID to capture date.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. If you use the capture date as the partition key, it sends all records that are generated on a given day to the same shard. This method would overload shards and not resolve hot shards that are caused by selecting an incorrect partition key, such as facility ID.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/key-concepts.html#partition-key"partition keys/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kinesis/latest/APIReference/API_PutRecord.html"how partition keys are used with PutRecord/a.

question_content: pAn ecommerce company plans to use Amazon EMR for big data analytics. The company requires a solution that has persistent storage that is independent of compute resources.pA data engineer wants to follow best practices to run cost-optimized workloads on Amazon EMR that maintain high performance standards.pWhich solution will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Graviton based Amazon EC2 instances. Use a mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances for the nodes. Use Amazon S3 as the persistent data store.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use Amazon EMR for data   processing, interactive analysis, and machine learning (ML). You can deploy workloads to Amazon EMR by using EC2 instances, among other services. Amazon EMR best practices recommend that you use Graviton based EC2 instances for cost savings, as well as a mix of On-Demand and Spot Instances for cost optimization. By having a mix of On-Demand and Spot instances, the workload is still able to get the high performance that is required. Amazon S3 is an object storage service. Amazon S3 is recommended for persistent storage because it is independent of Amazon EMR (compute) clusters.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ManagementGuide/emr-instance-purchasing-options.html"Amazon EMR instance purchasing options/a.pLearn more about href="https://aws.github.io/aws-emr-best-practices/docs/bestpractices/Cost%20Optimizations/best_practices/"Amazon EMR best practices for cost optimization/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Graviton based Amazon EC2 instances. Use Spot Instance for all the nodes. Use Amazon S3 as the persistent data store.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon S3 is an object storage service. Amazon S3 is recommended for persistent storage because it is independent of Amazon EMR (compute) clusters. EC2 Spot Instances give you the ability to purchase unused EC2 capacity at an often discounted price when compared to On-Demand prices. However, Spot Instances can be interrupted and shut down with a 2-minute notification. Amazon EMR best practices recommend that you use a mix of On-Demand and Spot Instances to optimize cost. If you use only Spot Instances for all nodes, you risk unexpected termination and loss of availability, which is a less-performant workload.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Graviton based Amazon EC2 instances. Use a mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances for the nodes. Use Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) as the persistent data store.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. HDFS is ephemeral and tied to the lifetime of the Amazon EMR (compute) cluster. Therefore, when a cluster is terminated, all data is lost. The question requires persistent storage independent of compute resources. For persistent storage independent of the cluster, Amazon S3 is recommended.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a compute-optimized Amazon EC2 instance family for primary nodes. Use a mix of On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances for the nodes. Use Hadoop Distributed File System (HDFS) as the persistent data store.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Compute optimized instances are good for applications that benefit from  high-performance processors. In this scenario, a compute-optimized instance is not necessary because primary nodes are not compute intensive. Additionally, an HDFS is ephemeral and does not provide the required persistent storage. Therefore, this combination does not follow best practices nor meet the requirements.pLearn more about href="https://aws.github.io/aws-emr-best-practices/docs/bestpractices/Cost%20Optimizations/best_practices/#bp-14-use-the-right-hardware-family-for-the-job-type"Amazon EMR hardware families/a.

question_content: pA media company wants to use Amazon OpenSearch Service to analyze real-time data about popular musical artists and songs. The company expects to ingest millions of new data events every day. The new data events will arrive through an Amazon Kinesis data stream. The company must transform the data and then ingest the data into the OpenSearch Service domain.pWhich method should the company use to ingest the data with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Data Firehose and an AWS Lambda function to transform the data and deliver the transformed data to OpenSearch Service.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Firehose is a fully managed service that delivers near real-time streaming data to different destinations, such as Amazon S3 and OpenSearch Service. This solution meets the requirements with minimum operational overhead because Firehose can automatically call a Lambda function to transform the records before it sends the data to the destination.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/what-is-this-service.html"Firehose/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a Logstash pipeline that has prebuilt filters to transform the data and deliver the transformed data to OpenSearch Service.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Logstash is an opensource tool that collects data in near real time and can send data to different destinations. This solution requires you to self-host and manage the Logstash agents. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirement of least operational overhead.pLearn more about href="https://aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/features/integration/"OpenSearch Service Integrations/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/managedomains-logstash.html"OpenSearch Service and Logstash/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an AWS Lambda function to call the Amazon Kinesis Agent to transform the data and deliver the transformed data OpenSearch Service.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Kinesis Agent is a software application that can collect data and send the data to a Kinesis data stream. Kinesis Agent cannot read data from the stream, which means that this option does not meet the requirements.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/writing-with-agents.html"how to use Kinesis Agent to write to Kinesis Data Streams/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse the Kinesis Client Library (KCL) to transform the data and deliver the transformed data to OpenSearch Service.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. KCL is a library that can be used to build applications that read data from Kinesis data streams. Although this solution is possible, this method requires more operational overhead to develop, deploy, and maintain the software when compared to using a Firehose stream.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/shared-throughput-kcl-consumers.html"how to use the KCL/a.

question_content: pA data engineer must build a data pipeline to process and analyze high volumes of clickstream events from a company's ecommerce application. The pipeline needs to ingest the streaming data, perform transformation, and load the transformed data into Amazon Redshift for analysis.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the application to send the streaming data to Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) Serverless. Connect an AWS Glue streaming extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to transform the data and store the data in Amazon S3. When an object is created, invoke an AWS Lambda function to load the transformed data into Amazon Redshift.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Amazon MSK to process streaming data that is compatible with Kafka. You need to modify the application to send the data to a Kafka stream. AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service that can help with data preparation. You can connect a streaming ETL job to a Kafka stream to transform the data and load the transformed data into Amazon S3. Then, you need a Lambda function to load the data into Amazon Redshift. This solution requires additional operational overhead because you use many services.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/msk/latest/developerguide/what-is-msk.html"Amazon MSK/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-job-streaming.html"streaming ETL jobs in AWS Glue/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the application to send the streaming data to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Add a subscription filter to forward the data to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to transform the data and store the data in Amazon S3. When an object is created, invoke a second Lambda function to load the transformed data into Amazon Redshift.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use CloudWatch Logs to centralize application logs by using a CloudWatch agent on the application host or by using the AWS SDK in code. After CloudWatch captures the clickstream data, you can set up a subscription filter to forward the data to Lambda. Lambda is a serverless compute service that you can use to run code without the need to provision or manage services. You can use Lambda to transform the data. However, this solution requires a second function to load data into Amazon Redshift. Therefore, this solution requires more operational overhead than a managed solution, such as Firehose. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/Subscriptions.html"real-time processing of log data with subscriptions/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the application to send the streaming data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Connect an Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (previously known as Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics) application to transform the data and store the data in Amazon S3. When an object is created, invoke an AWS Lambda function to load the transformed data into Amazon Redshift.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Kinesis Data Streams is a streaming service that you can use to stream data from multiple sources in near real time. You can ingest the data by using a Kinesis Agent on the application host or by using the AWS SDK in code. You can use Managed Service for Apache Flink to transform streaming data. You can integrate Managed Service for Apache Flink with a Kinesis Data Streams stream as a source. Managed Service for Apache Flink can send the transformed data to Amazon S3. Then, you need a Lambda function to load the data into Amazon Redshift. This solution requires more operational overhead than a managed solution such as Firehose. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managed-flink/latest/java/how-it-works.html"Managed Service for Apache Flink/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the application to send the streaming data to Amazon Data Firehose. Configure Firehose data transformation to invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform the incoming source data and load the transformed data into Amazon Redshift.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Firehose is a streaming service that you can use to stream data from multiple sources in near real time to multiple targets. You can ingest the data by using a Kinesis Agent on the application host or by using the AWS SDK in code. You can use a Lambda function to perform the necessary transformations on the incoming data before you send the data to Amazon Redshift. Firehose can handle high volumes of data and automatically scales to accommodate the load. Firehose has a built-in integration with Lambda and Amazon Redshift that provides the least operational overhead.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/data-transformation.html"how to use Firehose and Lambda for data transformation/a.

question_content: pA lab uses IoT sensors to monitor humidity, temperature, and pressure for a project. The sensors send 100 KB of data every 10 seconds. A downstream process will read the data from an Amazon S3 bucket every 30 seconds.  pWhich solution will deliver the data to the S3 bucket with the LEAST latency?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and Amazon Data Firehose to deliver the data to the S3 bucket. Use the default buffer interval for Firehose.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Kinesis Data Streams is a streaming service that you can use to store and ingest streaming data from multiple sources in near real time. Kinesis Data Streams can be configured to send data to a Firehose delivery stream. Firehose buffers deliver data in memory up until a certain buffering size and for a certain buffering interval. The buffering interval is dependent on the data destination. In this scenario, because the destination is Amazon S3, the default buffering interval is 300 seconds. The 300-second buffering interval does not meet the requirements in this scenario.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/buffering-hints.html"how to configure buffering sizes and buffering intervals on Firehose/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to deliver the data to the S3 bucket. Configure the stream to use 5 provisioned shards.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect.span style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit;" Kinesis Data Streams is a streaming service that you can use to store and ingest streaming data from multiple sources in near real time. Kinesis Data Streams does not natively deliver data to Amazon S3. Instead, you would typically use another service, such as Firehose, to transfer the data from Kinesis Data Streams to Amazon S3. Configuring provisioned shards is only used to set the read and write capacity.pLearn more about span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html"what you can do with Kinesis Data Streams/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and call the Kinesis Client Library to deliver the data to the S3 bucket. Use a 5 second buffer interval from an application.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Kinesis Data Streams is a streaming service that you can use to store and ingest streaming data from multiple sources in near real time. The KCL consumes and processes data from a Kinesis data stream and writes to destinations, such as Amazon S3. Using the SDK, a 5-second buffer interval can be set to meet the 30-second delivery requirement in near real time without adding additional latency. pLearn more about span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/introduction.html"what you can do with Kinesis Data Streams/a. pspan style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit;"Learn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/shared-throughput-kcl-consumers.html"how to use the KCL/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink (previously known as Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics) and Amazon Data Firehose to deliver the data to the S3 bucket. Use a 5 second buffer interval for Firehose.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Managed Service for Apache Flink to transform streaming data. However, using Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink still requires Kinesis Data Streams to receive data from the sensors. In this scenario, Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink would help to query and analyze the streaming data, but does not meet the goal of having the data delivered to the S3 bucket with the least latency. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/managed-flink/latest/java/how-it-works.html"how the managed service for Apache Flink works/a.

question_content: pA company uses Amazon Redshift to run SQL queries. The company has a table with the following columns: 'product_id', 'name', 'price', and 'category'. A data engineer wants to itemize the products based on price, and then create a ranked list of products based on price without duplicate ranks. Here is an example of the desired output:pproduct_1_id, product_1_name, 100, product_1_category 1pproduct_2_id, product_2_name, 90, product_2_category 2pproduct_3_id, product_3_name, 90, product_3_category 3pWhich SQL function or construct will achieve this goal?

answer_choices.choice_content: pSELECT product_id, name, price, category, p    COUNT(DISTINCT product_id) as product_rankbr  FROM tablepORDER BY pricebr
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. COUNT (DISTINCT emcolumn/em) calculates the number of different values that are in the introduced column. The goal in this scenario is to create a ranked list, not calculate the number of different products. Therefore, this option is not the correct construct to generate the desired output.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_COUNT.html"the COUNT function/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSELECT product_id, name, price, category,p    RANK() OVER (ORDER BY price) as product_rank br  FROM tablebr
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The RANK function assigns a rank for each record depending on the ORDER BY clause. In this scenario, if two records have the same value, then they will receive the same rank and the record that follows will skip one value. In this scenario, the RANK function is not a valid construct to meet the requirements because you need to rank a list without duplicate ranks.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_WF_RANK.html"the RANK function/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: p  p style="font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; font-size: 16px; font-family: Arial;"SELECT product_id, name, price, category,  p style="font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; font-size: 16px; font-family: Arial;"    COUNT(product_id) as product_rankbr    FROM table  p style="font-style: normal; font-variant-ligatures: normal; font-variant-caps: normal; font-weight: 400; font-size: 16px; font-family: Arial;"ORDER BY price
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. COUNT (DISTINCT emcolumn/em) calculates the number of values that are in the introduced column. The goal in this scenario is to create a ranked list, not calculate the number of products. Therefore, this option is not the correct construct to generate the desired output.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_COUNT.html"the COUNT function/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSELECT product_id, name, price, category,br      ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY price) AS product_rankbr  FROM table
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse on which you can run SQL queries. The ROW_NUMBER function assigns a unique row number to each row in the result set based on the specified order. In this scenario, the row number is the product price.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_WF_ROW_NUMBER.html"the ROW_NUMBER function/a.

question_content: pA finance company receives data from third-party data providers and stores the data as objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. pThe company ran an AWS Glue crawler on the objects to create a data catalog. The AWS Glue crawler created multiple tables. However, the company expected that the crawler would create only one table. pThe company needs a solution that will ensure the AWS Glue crawler creates only one table.pWhich combination of solutions will meet this requirement? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the object format, compression type, and schema are the same for each object.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An AWS Glue crawler is used to automatically create tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. For the AWS Glue to crawler create a single table for data sources in Amazon S3, the data must have the same underlying S3 partition structure, format (CSV, Apache Parquet, or JSON), compression type (Snappy, gzip, or bzip2), and schema. Therefore, ensuring that the object format, compression type, and schema is the same for each object helps prevent the AWS Glue crawler from creating multiple tables.pbr class="Apple-interchange-newline"  Learn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html"AWS /aspan style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html"span style="text-decoration: underline;"Glue crawlers/a. pLearn more about span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/glue-crawler-multiple-tables"why AWS Glue crawlers create multiple tables/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the object format and schema are the same for each object. Do not enforce consistency for the compression type of each object.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An AWS Glue crawler is used to automatically create tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. For the AWS Glue crawler to create a single table for data sources in Amazon S3, the data must have the same underlying S3 partition structure, format (CSV, Apache Parquet, or JSON), compression type (Snappy, gzip, or bzip2), and schema. Ensuring that the object format and schema are the same for each object is a requirement for the crawler to create a single table. However, if the objects do not also have a consistent compression type, the crawler creates multiple tables.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the schema is the same for each object. Do not enforce consistency for the file format and compression type of each object.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An AWS Glue crawler is used to automatically create tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. For the AWS Glue crawler to create a single table for data sources in Amazon S3, the data must have the same underlying S3 partition structure, format (CSV, Apache Parquet, or JSON), compression type (Snappy, gzip, or bzip2), and schema. Ensuring that the schema is the same for the objects is a requirement for the crawler to create a single table. However, if the objects do not also have a consistent file format and compression type, the crawler creates multiple tables.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that the structure of the prefix for each S3 object name is consistent.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. An AWS Glue crawler is used to automatically create tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. For the AWS Glue crawler to create a single table for data sources in Amazon S3, the data must have the same underlying S3 partition structure, format (CSV, Apache Parquet, or JSON), compression type (Snappy, gzip, or bzip2), and schema. Therefore, to prevent the AWS Glue crawler from creating multiple tables, you should ensure the structure of the prefix for each S3 object name is consistent.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html"AWS Glue crawlers/a.pLearn more about href="https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/glue-crawler-multiple-tables"why AWS Glue crawlers create multiple tables/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pEnsure that all S3 object names follow a similar pattern.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. An AWS Glue crawler is used to automatically create tables in the AWS Glue Data Catalog. For the AWS Glue crawler to create a single table for data sources in Amazon S3, the data must have the same underlying S3 partition structure, format (CSV, Apache Parquet, or JSON), compression type (Snappy, gzip, or bzip2), and schema. Ensuring that all the S3 object names follow a similar pattern does not affect whether the Glue crawler creates multiple tables.

question_content: pA company is building a new data platform on AWS to understand the trends of its customer service business. The company has ingested 3 years of customer service data into Amazon S3. The data is in CSV format. The data is partitioned across multiple files of the same size. The data is compressed with gzip. The company needs the entire history of the data for the analysis.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon EMR cluster with Hive installed. Set up an external Hive metastore in the cluster to build the schema and tables from the S3 data. Use an Amazon Athena data connector with the external Hive metastore. Use Athena to query the data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Amazon EMR to manage the compute capacity necessary to run big data frameworks including Hive. Hive is an analytics package that runs on top of a Hadoop cluster in Amazon EMR. You can use Hive to create table and schema metadata that match your data in Amazon S3. Athena is a serverless service that can directly query data in Amazon S3. Athena needs to reference schema and table metadata from the data to be able to query S3 data. Therefore, you can use external Hive metastores with an Athena data connector to reference the metadata and query the S3 data. This solution requires additional operational overhead. You need to create and select the right configuration in the EMR cluster, the Hive metastore, and the Athena data connector to be able to query the data. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/emr/latest/ReleaseGuide/emr-hive.html"Amazon EMR and Hive/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/connect-to-data-source-hive.html"how to use an Athena data connector with the external Hive metastore/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/catalog-and-crawler.html"Data Catalog and crawlers/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/serverless-whatis.html"Redshift Serverless/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDefine and run a crawler in AWS Glue to populate AWS Glue Data Catalog from the partitioned data. Create a new Amazon Redshift Serverless endpoint. Define an external schema and tables by using the Data Catalog. Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query the data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use AWS Glue to create and run crawlers to automatically extract the metadata and create table definitions in the Data Catalog. The crawlers can run across data that can be partitioned and compressed. Redshift Serverless is a cloud data warehouse that automatically provisions compute capacity and intelligently scales the resources necessary for the queries to run. You can use Redshift Serverless to query data in Amazon S3 by using Redshift Spectrum. Redshift Spectrum can use existent entries in the Data Catalog during the creation of the external schema and tables. This solution gives you the ability to directly query the S3 data. This solution requires the least operational overhead. You use serverless AWS services and the Data Catalog to query the partitioned and compressed data with minimal effort. Additionally, you use automatic AWS Glue and Amazon Redshift capabilities.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/catalog-and-crawler.html"Data Catalog and crawlers/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/serverless-whatis.html"Redshift Serverless/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/c-using-spectrum.html"how to query external data by using Redshift Spectrum/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an Amazon Redshift cluster and use an AWS Glue job to ingest the S3 data into Amazon Redshift tables. Use Amazon Redshift to query the data.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use AWS Glue to create extract, transform, and load (ETL) jobs from S3 data to ingest the data into Amazon Redshift. Amazon Redshift is a cloud data warehouse that you can use to query data for analytics purposes. This solution requires additional operational overhead. You need to create a Redshift provisioned cluster with the necessary configuration to run the analytics queries. You need to create the ingestion job to ingest the data into the Redshift cluster. A solution that uses only serverless services would require less operational overhead. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-connect-redshift-home.html"Amazon Redshift connections in AWS Glue/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-partitions.html"how to manage partitions for ETL output in AWS Glue/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/serverless-console-comparison.html"the comparison between Redshift Serverless and an Amazon Redshift provisioned data warehouse/a.

question_content: pA financial technology company offers a promotion to new users that promises no additional transaction fees on any transactions that are completed in the first 30 days. The company uses Amazon DynamoDB to store transaction data and AWS Lambda to process transactions. The company wants to manage the lifecycle of the promotional transaction data efficiently. question_content: pA data engineer notices that Amazon Athena queries are held in a queue before the queries run.pHow can the data engineer prevent the queries from queueing?

answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Using provisioned capacity in Athena allows for the allocation of dedicated resources to queries. This action can help reduce queuing delays because provisioned capacity ensures that sufficient resources are available to process queries promptly. Provisioned capacity is a practical solution to address the queuing issue and enhance overall query performance in Athena.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/capacity-management-requirements.html"Athena capacity management/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse federated queries.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Federated queries are used to query data from multiple sources. They are not directly related to addressing queuing delays in Athena. answer_choices.choice_content: pAllow users who run the Athena queries to an existing workgroup.

The maximum concurrent calls   per second limit in Athena is 20 by default. Exceeding 20 concurrent calls per second might increase the number of queries in the queue. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/service-limits.html"Athena service quotas/a. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ugerformance-tuning.html"performance tuning in Athena/a.

question_content: pA data engineer at a healthcare company must set up a secure environment on AWS to manage patient records. The data must be stored in Amazon DynamoDB, and must be encrypted at rest to meet regulatory compliance.pWhich solutions encrypt data in DynamoDB in a secure manner? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) in DynamoDB tables.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS KMS is a service that is used to create, store, and manage cryptographic keys. Server-side encryption is the encryption of data at its destination by the application or service that receives it. AWS KMS is integrated with DynamoDB to support encryption at rest. With this feature, DynamoDB automatically encrypts all data before it is written to disk and decrypts it when retrieved. This action provides a seamless encryption mechanism for data at rest.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/services-dynamodb.html"how DynamoDB uses AWS KMS/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse client-side encryption prior to uploading items to DynamoDB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Client-side encryption ensures that data is encrypted on the client side before it is sent to DynamoDB. With client-side encryption, the sensitive data is encrypted in transit, which meets the requirements.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/EncryptionAtRest.html"DynamoDB encryption at rest/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pStore an encryption key in a private Git repository to provide access for team members.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. It is not recommended to store sensitive materials like encryption keys in any version control system—even in private repositories. Encryption keys should be managed through dedicated key management systems like AWS KMS.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/getting-started.html"how to manage keys in AWS KMS/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Lambda to automatically decrypt data every time the data is accessed from DynamoDB.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. This approach introduces unnecessary complexities like having to ensure the proper permissions of Lambda, manage potential failures, and handle effective logging. Decryption every time the data is accessed opens a window where the data, after it is decrypted, can be exposed to potential breaches—especially if subsequent processes do not handle this decrypted data securely. AWS provides best practices for securing sensitive data, such as encryption and decryption processes.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.comrescriptive-guidance/latest/encryption-best-practices/welcome.html"encryption best practices/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS Lambda to rotate AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys that are used with DynamoDB on a weekly basis.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although Lambda can be used for a variety of automation tasks within AWS, manually rotating encryption keys on such a frequent basis by using a Lambda function is not a recommended or common practice. Manual rotation, especially on a weekly basis, could lead to operational complexities, increased risk of errors, and potential misconfigurations—especially if the rotation process is not thoroughly tested and monitored. Moreover, frequent manual key rotation might not necessarily provide enhanced security. Instead, manual key rotation could lead to issues with data access if the manual key rotation is not handled correctly.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/best-practices.html#rotate-keys"AWS KMS best practices/a.

question_content: pA company has created a solution that deploys applications by using AWS CloudFormation. answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure CloudFormation to send the event data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use AWS Glue to transform the events to Apache ORC format. Create permissions for the auditors to run Amazon Athena SQL queries on the S3 bucket.

However, you cannot configure CloudFormation to deliver logs to Amazon S3. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/troubleshooting.html"CloudFormation logs/a. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-etl-format-orc-home.html"how to use the Apache ORC format in AWS Glue/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/using-athena-sql.html"how to use Athena SQL/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pDetermine the log group names for the CloudFormation event data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create permissions for the auditors to run CloudWatch Logs Insights queries on the specific CloudFormation log group names.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use CloudWatch Logs Insights to interactively search and analyze log data in CloudWatch Logs, including logs that CloudFormation generates. However, the CloudWatch Logs Insights query syntax does not support SQL. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData.html"how to analyze log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate a new AWS CloudTrail trail to capture the API calls being produced by the federated identity provider. Configure the trail to deliver the events in Apache ORC format to Amazon S3. Create permissions for the auditors to run Amazon Athena SQL queries on the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use Athena SQL to query data in an S3 bucket. However, CloudTrail delivers events in a row-based JSON format to an S3 bucket. You cannot configure the events in any other format. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-create-a-trail-using-the-console-first-time.html"how to create a trail in CloudTrail/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/using-athena-sql.html"how to use Athena SQL/a.

question_content: pA company loads sales data into an Amazon S3 bucket every day. The company configured the S3 bucket to use an S3 PUT event trigger to invoke an AWS Lambda function that performs an inventory measurement process when the company uploads objects to the bucket. The inventory measurement process writes results back to the original S3 bucket.pWhen the company uploads sales data, the inventory measurement process repeats continuously until the company manually stops the process.pThe company needs a solution to ensure that the inventory measurement process will run only once when the company uploads new objects.pWhich solution will meet this requirement?

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CloudTrail events to invoke the Lambda function instead of the S3 PUT event.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. CloudTrail is a service that provides a record of actions taken by a user, a role, or an AWS service. span style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit;"CloudTrail events for Amazon S3 is an alternate approach to receive events for PutObject to an S3 bucket. Configuring this method instead of S3 PUT event trigger does not solve the issue with continuous repetition of the process. This method does not solve the issue because this configuration will continue to create a new CloudTrail event each time the inventory measurement process writes output to the same bucket.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-logging-s3-info.html"S3 CloudTrail events/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure Amazon S3 events to invoke an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue to write only once.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon SQS FIFO queues are designed to enhance messaging between applications when the order of operations and events is critical, or where duplicates are not allowed. However, Amazon SQS FIFO queues are not compatible with S3 events .pspan style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit;"Learn more about span style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit; text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-fifo-queues.html"Amazon SQS FIFO queues/aspan style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit;". pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/FIFO-compatibility.html"Amazon SQS FIFO queue compatibility/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse a service control policy (SCP) to prevent continuous daily writes to the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Organizations is an account management service that enables you to consolidate multiple AWS accounts into an organization that you create and centrally manage. SCPs are policies that are used to manage permissions in your AWS organization. span style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit;"You can use an SCP to specify the maximum permissions of IAM users and roles to write to an S3 bucket. However, an SCP cannot detect and prevent a continuous write process.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html"SCPs/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse one S3 bucket to store sales data, and use a second S3 bucket to store inventory process output.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. span style="font-family: inherit; font-size: inherit; font-style: inherit; font-variant-ligatures: inherit; font-variant-caps: inherit; font-weight: inherit;"If you configure the inventory output result to be written to the same S3 bucket, then the function indirectly triggers itself and the process keeps repeating itself. Using a second S3 bucket to store inventory process output ensures that the process does not run in an execution loop because your second S3 bucket does not invoke the Lambda process that is configured in the first Amazon S3 bucket.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html"Amazon S3 Event Notification/a.

question_content: pA company recently moved its data lake to AWS. The data lake is built on Amazon S3. The data lake is managed and secured by using AWS Lake Formation. A data engineer must configure a solution that captures all Lake Formation events. The solution must be able to analyze the events at scale through queries and generate an audit report by using Amazon QuickSight.pWhich combination of steps will meet the requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Select TWO.)

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CloudTrail Lake to create an event data store. Enable management and data events. Select Lake Formation, and then Log all events under Data Events.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Lake Formation is used to manage access controls for data that is stored in your data lake. Lake Formation is integrated with CloudTrail to log actions. CloudTrail Lake is a managed data lake that you can use to store, access, and analyze user and API activity in AWS. You can use data events to log resource operations that are performed on or within a resource. You can use CloudTrail Lake to run SQL-based queries on events for audit purposes. This solution captures all Lake Formation events and analyzes them at scale through queries. However, CloudTrail Lake is not a supported data source that is used to create the dataset in QuickSight.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.html"CloudTrail Lake/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CloudTrail to create a trail. Enable management and data events. Select Lake Formation, and then Log all events under Data Events. In CloudTrail event history, create a table in Amazon Athena.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Lake Formation is a service that is used to manage access controls for data that is stored in your data lake. CloudTrail is used to monitor and track user and API activity in your AWS account. Lake Formation is integrated with CloudTrail Lake to capture management operations that are performed on AWS resources. You must create a trail for an ongoing record of events in your AWS account. You can use data events to log resource operations that are performed on or within a resource. After you create the trail, you can go to the CloudTrail event history to create a table in Athena. Athena is a serverless interactive query service that is used to analyze data in Amazon S3 by using standard SQL. This solution captures all Lake Formation events. With Athena, you can analyze the data at scale through queries. You can also create the audit report in QuickSight by using Athena as the data source during dataset creation.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/logging-using-cloudtrail.html"how to log Lake Formation API calls by using CloudTrail/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/cloudtrail-logs.html"how to query CloudTrail logs/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/supported-data-sources.html"data sources that are supported by QuickSight/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse AWS CloudTrail to create a trail. Enable management and data events. Select Lake Formation. and then Log all events under Data Events. Build a serverless, event-driven workflow with AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) and crawler to add the table to the catalog.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Lake Formation is a service that is used to manage access controls for data that is stored in your data lake. CloudTrail is used to monitor and track user and API activity in your AWS account. Lake Formation is integrated with CloudTrail Lake to capture management operations that are performed on AWS resources. You must create a trail for an ongoing record of events in your AWS account. You can use Data Events to log resource operations that are performed on or within a resource. AWS Glue is a serverless data integration service that you can use to move, prepare, and integrate data from multiple sources. This solution requires additional operational overhead because after you create the trail, you have to build and invoke your own serverless workflow by using AWS Glue to add the table to the catalog.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lake-formation/latest/dg/logging-using-cloudtrail.html"how to log Lake Formation API calls by using CloudTrail/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/cloudtrail-logs.html"how to query CloudTrail logs/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse QuickSight to create a dataset by using Amazon Athena as the data source. Create the report.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. QuickSight is a business intelligence service that is used to create dashboards for reports. Athena is a serverless interactive query service that is used to analyze data in Amazon S3 by using standard SQL. With Athena, you can run queries on logs. Then you can integrate the query results with QuickSight as the data source to provide the data to create the report. This solution meets the requirements to create an audit report in QuickSight.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/create-a-data-set-athena.html"how to create a dataset by using Athena/a. pLearn more about span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/supported-data-sources.html"data sources that are supported by QuickSight/a.div

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse QuickSight to create a dataset by using AWS CloudTrail Lake as the data source. Create the report.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. QuickSight is a business intelligence service that is used to create dashboards for reports. You can use CloudTrail Lake to run SQL-based queries on your events   for audit purposes. CloudTrail Lake is not a supported data source that is used to create the dataset in QuickSight.

question_content: pA company has a business intelligence platform on AWS. The company uses an AWS Storage Gateway Amazon S3 File Gateway to transfer files from the company's on-premises environment to an Amazon S3 bucket. pA data engineer needs to set up a process that will automatically launch an AWS Glue workflow to run a series of AWS Glue jobs when each file transfer finishes successfully.pWhich solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

answer_choices.choice_content: pDetermine when the file transfers usually finish based on previous successful file transfers. Set up an Amazon EventBridge scheduled event to initiate the AWS Glue jobs at that time of day.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. EventBridge gives you the ability to build loosely coupled, event-driven architectures. Setting up a scheduled event in EventBridge based on previous file transfer times does not guarantee that the scheduled event will begin only when the file transfer finished successfully. You can have a file transfer that is shorter or longer than previous file transfer times. If a file delivery occurs outside of the scheduled time, the file is not processed until the next scheduled time.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-events.html"EventBridge events/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up an Amazon EventBridge event that initiates the AWS Glue workflow after every successful S3 File Gateway file transfer event.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. EventBridge is used to detect events from AWS services and initiate workflows in response. EventBridge supports notifications from AWS Storage Gateway for file transfer completion events. Supporting notifications gives you the ability to initiate an AWS Glue workflow automatically after each file transfer event without additional operational overhead. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/Main_monitoring-gateways-common.html"how to monitor AWS Storage Gateway/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up an on-demand AWS Glue workflow so that the data engineer can start the AWS Glue workflow when each file transfer is complete.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Glue workflows are a flow of AWS Glue jobs and crawlers that are used to manage complex extract, transform, and load (ETL) activities in AWS Glue. Configuring the AWS Glue workflow to only start by having the data engineer manually initiate the workflow after each file transfer adds operational overhead. Therefore, this solution does not meet the requirement of least operational overhead.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/workflows_overview.html"AWS Glue workflows/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSet up an AWS Lambda function that will invoke the AWS Glue Workflow. Set up an event for the creation of an S3 object as a trigger for the Lambda function.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Lambda is a service that gives you the ability to run code without managing the underlying infrastructure. However, you would need to add additional logic to the Lambda code to trigger the AWS Glue workflow, which would add operational overhead to create and maintain this functionality.  div  Learn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-functions.html"Lambda functions/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/workflows_overview.html"AWS Glue workflows/a.

question_content: pA call center for a banking application receives multiple reports from users who are not able to access their bank accounts. After an initial analysis, the security team identified a change in the AWS WAF web access control list (ACL) that might be too restrictive because it is stopping some legitimate requests. A data engineer must provide a solution that identifies these false positives in the AWS WAF logs.pWhich solution is the MOST efficient?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the logs to be sent to Amazon Data Firehose. Forward the logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Identify the false positives by using OpenSearch Service Dashboards.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS WAF is a web application firewall. Firehose is a streaming service that can forward data to Amazon OpenSearch. OpenSearch Service is a search engine that is used to index and search logs. However, this solution requires the creation and ongoing management of an OpenSearch Service cluster. Therefore, this solution is not the most efficient.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/logging-kinesis.html"how to send AWS WAF logs to Firehose/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-destination.html#create-destination-elasticsearch"how to choose OpenSearch Service for your Firehose destination/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/dashboards.html"how to use OpenSearch Dashboards with OpenSearch Service/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the logs to be sent to Amazon Data Firehose. Forward the logs to Amazon Redshift. Identify the false positives by using the Amazon Redshift query editor.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS WAF is a web application firewall. Firehose is a streaming service that can forward data to Amazon Redshift. Amazon Redshift is a data warehouse service with a built-in query editor. However, this solution requires the creation and ongoing management of an Amazon Redshift cluster. Therefore, this solution is not the most efficient.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/logging-kinesis.html"how to send AWS WAF logs to Firehose/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-destination.html#create-destination-redshift"how to choose Amazon Redshift for your Firehose destination/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/query-editor.html"how to query a database by using the Amazon Redshift query editor/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the logs to be sent to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Identify the false positives by using the Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights query editor.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. AWS WAF is a web application firewall. Amazon CloudWatch is a monitoring service that is integrated with many AWS services. AWS WAF logs can be sent to CloudWatch Logs. CloudWatch Logs Insights provides an interface to interactively search logs. CloudWatch Logs Insights is also embedded directly in the AWS WAF administrator console with a number of prebuilt query samples for AWS WAF logs. This solution is the most efficient.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/logging-cw-logs.html"how to send AWS WAF logs to CloudWatch Logs/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/AnalyzingLogData.html"how to analyze log data with CloudWatch Logs Insights/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure the logs to be sent to Amazon S3. Define and run an AWS Glue crawler to create an AWS Glue Data Catalog. Identify the false positives by using the Amazon Athena query editor.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS WAF is a web application firewall. AWS WAF logs can be sent to Amazon S3. AWS Glue is a serverless multi-function data analytics service. AWS Glue can be used to extract metadata information from S3 objects, such as the AWS WAF logs. Athena can be used to query a data catalog produced by AWS Glue by using standard SQL. However, this solution requires configuring and scheduling AWS Glue crawlers and writing queries from scratch in Athena. Therefore, this solution is not the most efficient.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/logging-s3.html"how to send AWS WAF logs to Amazon S3/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/add-crawler.html"how to define crawlers in AWS Glue/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/using-athena-sql.html"how to use Athena SQL/a.

question_content: pA company has an Amazon Redshift stored procedure named Daily_Aggr_SP. The stored procedure takes the date as an input to insert daily aggregated data into a production table on demand.pWhich SQL statement will run the Daily_Aggr_SP stored procedure?

answer_choices.choice_content: pspan style="font-family: Courier New"CALL Daily_Aggr_SP('2023-01-01')
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The CALL statement is used to invoke a stored procedure in Amazon Redshift. The syntax is CALL procedure_name(argument list). This statement runs the Daily_Aggr_SP stored procedure and passes the date parameter. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_CALL_procedure.html"the CALL statement in Amazon Redshift/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pspan style="font-family: Courier New"FETCH Daily_Aggr_SP('2023-01-01')
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. FETCH is not a valid statement to use to invoke a stored procedure in Amazon Redshift SQL. FETCH is used to retrieve a portion of rows that are returned by a query. This statement cannot be used to run a stored procedure. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/fetch.html"the FETCH statement in Amazon Redshift/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pspan style="font-family: Courier New"SHOW PROCEDURE Daily_Aggr_SP('2023-01-01')
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The SHOW PROCEDURE statement is used to list the definition of a stored procedure in Amazon Redshift. This statement does not run the stored procedure. To invoke a stored procedure, you must use the CALL statement. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_SHOW_PROCEDURE.html"the SHOW PROCEDURE statement in Amazon Redshift/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pspan style="font-family: Courier New"SELECT Daily_Aggr_SP('2023-01-01')
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The SELECT statement is used to retrieve data from a table or view in Amazon Redshift. This statement cannot be used to run a stored procedure. To invoke a stored procedure, you must use the CALL statement. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/r_SELECT_synopsis.html"SELECT statement in Amazon Redshift/a.

question_content: pA company stores business-critical data in an Amazon S3 bucket. To meet legal requirements, a data engineer needs to ensure that the files are stored for at least 2 years. The files cannot be deleted during the 2-year period.pWhich configuration will meet these requirements?

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure S3 Object Lock in compliance mode and set a 2-year retention period.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. You can use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode to prevent the deletion of files by any user, including the root user of the AWS account. A retention period determines the duration in which deletions cannot occur. A solution that configures the retention policy for 2 years meets the requirements.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lock-overview.html"S3 Object Lock/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an S3 bucket policy that explicitly denies delete permission to all IAM users and roles.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use an S3 bucket policy to grant permissions to an S3 bucket and to the objects that you store in the bucket. You can use an S3 bucket policy to prevent the deletion of the files. However, an authorized user can change the bucket policy to allow the deletion of files. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/bucket-policies.html"S3 bucket policies/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure an S3 Lifecycle policy that transitions files to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use an S3 Lifecycle policy to manage the lifecycle of an object to transition to different storage classes or to expire an object. A solution that transitions the object to S3 Glacier Deep Archive does not prevent the deletion of files.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/object-lifecycle-mgmt.html"how to manage your storage lifecycle/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pConfigure multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete to prevent users from accidentally deleting files from the bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. MFA delete provides additional security to prevent the accidental deletion of objects. However, a user with the appropriate MFA authentication could still delete the files. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiFactorAuthenticationDelete.html"how to configure MFA delete/a.

question_content: pA data engineer finished testing an Amazon Redshift stored procedure that processes and inserts data into a table that is not mission critical. The engineer wants to automatically run the stored procedure on a daily basis.pWhich solution will meet this requirement in the MOST cost-effective way?

answer_choices.choice_content: pCreate an AWS Lambda function to schedule a cron job to run the stored procedure.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Although you can run the stored procedure with the Redshift Data API using a Lambda function, Lambda functions themselves cannot schedule cron jobs. Instead, you must add Amazon EventBridge to the architecture to be able to schedule cron jobs. There is a cost that is associated with each function invocation. This solution is not the most cost effective. pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/how-aws-pricing-works/lambda.html"Lambda pricing/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/data-api-calling-event-bridge.html"how to use EventBridge to schedule Redshift Data API calls/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSchedule and run the stored procedure by using the Amazon Redshift Data API in an Amazon EC2 Spot Instance.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use the built-in Redshift Data API to run queries on Amazon Redshift tables. You can use the Data API to run a stored procedure. However, there is an additional cost that is associated with using an EC2 instance, regardless of the instance pricing model. Therefore, this method is not the most cost effective.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-spot-instances.html"Spot Instance pricing/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/how-aws-pricing-works/amazon-ec2.html"EC2 instance pricing/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse query editor v2 to run the stored procedure on a schedule.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. Query editor v2 is a built-in feature of Amazon Redshift. The query editor provides scheduling functionality at no extra cost. Amazon EventBridge starts the scheduled SQL statements. The Redshift Data API invokes the scheduled SQL statements at your desired time interval. This solution is the most cost-effective method because the solution uses features that are already provided by Amazon Redshift.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/mgmt/query-editor-v2-schedule-query.html"the query editor and scheduling statements/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pSchedule an AWS Glue Python shell job to run the stored procedure.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. AWS Glue Python shell jobs can be used for extract, transform, and load (ETL) jobs to process and insert data into a table. However, there is an additional cost associated with AWS Glue jobs. Therefore, this solution is not the most cost-effective method.pLearn more about href="https://aws.amazon.com/gluericing/"AWS Glue pricing/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/aws-glue-programming-python.html"how to use Python with AWS Glue/a.

question_content: pA data engineer frequently uses an Amazon Athena table to query a partitioned table that is in an Amazon S3 bucket. The data engineer recently deleted one of the S3 partitions manually. Then the data engineer attempted to refresh the Athena table. However, the data engineer received the following error message: "Partitions missing from file system." pThe data engineer   needs to resolve the error and to refresh the table so that Athena can successfully query the table.pWhich solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

answer_choices.choice_content: pRun a MSCK REPAIR TABLE statement multiple times until the error disappears.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Running MSCK REPAIR TABLE does not remove partitions from metadata that has already been removed manually from Amazon S3. The MSCK REPAIR TABLE statement only adds partitions to metadata.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/msck-repair-table.html#"MSCK REPAIR TABLE/a.pLearn more about span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/troubleshooting-athena.html#troubleshooting-athena-msck-repair-table"how to troubleshoot missing partitions in Athena/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pWrite a Python script that will add the missing partition path to the S3 bucket.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Writing a Python script to add missing partition paths is a programmatic approach, which is not the most operationally efficient solution. This solution can also introduce unnecessary complexity. Custom scripts require additional development and maintenance overhead. Additionally, this solution implies a missing partition. To fix this problem, you must remove the stale partition, not add a missing partition. pLearn more about href="https://boto3.amazonaws.com/v1/documentation/api/latest/reference/services/s3/clientut_object.html"put_object in Boto3 (SDK for Python)/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pUse an ALTER TABLE DROP PARTITION statement to remove the stale partition.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. In Athena, using ALTER TABLE DROP PARTITION is a straightforward way to remove the specific stale partitions and refresh the table for querying. This method gives you the ability to efficiently drop only the missing partitions.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/alter-table-drop-partition.html"ALTER TABLE DROP PARTITION/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRun a VACUUM statement to remove the stale partition.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Running a VACUUM statement is not used to manage partitions in Athena. The VACUUM statement is used to compact the underlying data files and reclaim space. question_content: pA retail company uses Amazon Redshift as a data warehouse to store historical sales, transaction, inventory, and customer data. question_content: pA data engineer wants to improve the performance of a long-running query in Amazon Redshift. The query involves joining two tables that are in a parent-child relationship. Both tables are very large and were created using the EVEN distribution style.pThe data engineer must redefine the tables to improve query performance.pWhich solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answer_choices.choice_content: pRecreate the parent table with an ALL distribution style. Leave the child table with the EVEN distribution style.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The ALL distribution style places a copy of the entire parent table on the first slice of each node in the Redshift cluster. The EVEN distribution style randomly distributes an even number of rows in the child table across all the slices on the nodes. This solution would ensure that the data from the parent table is available on each node to improve the join performance for the query. However, this solution would incur additional storage costs for the large parent table. A more cost-effective solution would be to create both tables with a KEY distribution style by using the column that the tables are joined on.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRecreate the child table with an ALL distribution style. Leave the parent table with the EVEN distribution style
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The ALL distribution style places a copy of the entire parent table on the first slice of each node in the Redshift cluster. The EVEN distribution style randomly distributes an even number of rows in the child table across all the slices on the nodes. This solution would ensure that the data from the child table is available on each node to improve the join performance for the query. However, this solution would incur additional storage costs for the large child table. A more cost-effective solution would be to create both tables with a KEY distribution style by using the column that the tables are joined on.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRecreate the parent table with a KEY distribution style based on the primary key. Recreate the child table with a KEY distribution style by using the matching join column.
answer_choices.solution_content: pCorrect. The KEY distribution style places rows of both tables across the slices in the nodes in the Redshift cluster based on the values in the selected column. Matching values are placed in the same node slice. A solution that distributes tables in a parent-child relationship by using the KEY distribution method with the joining column will physically collocate the row data from each table. A solution that collocates the related data will improve the query performance. Additionally, the KEY distribution style does not replicate data across the nodes. Therefore, this solution is the most cost-effective.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/c_choosing_dist_sort.html"distribution styles in Amazon Redshift/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pRecreate the parent table with a KEY distribution style based on the primary key. Recreate the child table with an EVEN distribution style.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. The KEY distribution style places rows in the parent table across the slices in the nodes in the Redshift cluster based on the values in the selected column. The EVEN distribution style randomly distributes an even number of rows in the child table across all the slices on the nodes. Both the KEY and EVEN distribution styles do not replicate data across multiple nodes. However, the related rows will not be collocated. Therefore, rows from one of the tables would need to be redistributed during query processing. This solution will not improve the query performance and does not meet the requirements.

question_content: pA company wants to visualize sales data that comes from multiple sources. The company needs to prototype a data visualization solution on AWS. Additionally, this solution is less suitable for a prototype because a prototype should be simple and flexible.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/enabling-access-redshift.html"connections from QuickSight to Amazon Redshift/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pIngest the data into an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon Athena table based on the S3 data. Create a dataset within Amazon QuickSight by using the Athena table as a data source. Visualize the data directly in QuickSight.

QuickSight is a serverless business intelligence service that you can use to create data visualizations. You can use Athena tables as a data source for QuickSight. This solution eliminates the need to manage a data warehouse and load data into the data warehouse. Therefore, this is the solution with the least operational overhead. pLearn more about   span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/what-is.html"Athena/a.pLearn more about   href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/create-a-data-set-athena.html"how to create a dataset by using Athena data/a.pLearn more about   span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/quicksight/latest/user/creating-data-sets.html"how to create datasets in QuickSight/a.

question_content: pAn online retail company has an application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances that are in a VPC. The company wants to collect flow logs for the VPC and analyze network traffic.pWhich solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

answer_choices.choice_content: pPublish flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use Amazon Athena for analytics.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use CloudWatch Logs to monitor and store log files from EC2 instances and other AWS sources. You can publish flow logs from your VPC in JSON format. You can use CloudWatch Logs to store and analyze log files. However, a solution that queries JSON log files by using Athena incurs additional costs. Therefore, this solution is not the most cost-effective. Athena is more suitable to query data formats such as Parquet.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/WhatIsCloudWatchLogs.html"CloudWatch Logs/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ugarsing-JSON.html"how to query JSON data in Athena/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/when-should-i-use-ate.html"when to use Athena/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPublish flow logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Use an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for analytics.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. You can use CloudWatch Logs to monitor and store log files from EC2 instances and other AWS sources. You can publish flow logs from your VPC in JSON format. You can use CloudWatch Logs to store and analyze log files. OpenSearch Service is a managed service that you can use to operate OpenSearch clusters. OpenSearch Service requires you to run and maintain a cluster. A solution that uses an OpenSearch Service cluster for analytics can be more expensive than a solution that uses Athena. Therefore, this solution is not the most cost-effective.pLearn more about span style="text-decoration-line: underline;"a target="_blank" href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/WhatIsCloudWatchLogs.html"CloudWatch Logs/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/what-is.html"OpenSearch Service/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPublish flow logs to Amazon S3 in text format. Use Amazon Athena for analytics.
answer_choices.solution_content: pIncorrect. Amazon S3 is an object storage service. Athena is a query service that you can use to query data that is stored in S3 buckets by using SQL. A solution that stores the flow logs in text format and uses Athena for analytics is not the most cost-effective. A solution that uses Athena to query text files is less efficient and generally costs more than a solution that uses columnar formats such as Parquet. Parquet also provides compression and encoding optimizations that can reduce costs.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/supported-serdes.html"supported data formats in Athena/a.pLearn more about href="https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/when-should-i-use-ate.html"when to use Athena/a.

answer_choices.choice_content: pPublish flow logs to Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format. Use Amazon Athena for analytics.
